briefBio: Our Lady of Loreto honors Mary in connection with the Holy House tradition and the mystery of the Incarnation lived in the home of Nazareth. The memorial invites prayer for households, pilgrims, and all who seek Christ with Mary.

name: Saint Damasus I, Pope
briefBio: Saint Damasus I, Pope is honored for pastoral service to the Church as Bishop of Rome. The celebration recalls a life spent guarding faith, worship, and communion.

name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
briefBio: Our Lady of Guadalupe honors Mary under this feast, title, or mystery in the Church calendar. It invites devotion to her place in the life of Christ and her maternal care for the Church.

name: Saint Peter Canisius, Priest and Doctor of the Church
briefBio: Saint Peter Canisius, Priest and Doctor of the Church is honored as a teacher of the faith whose writings helped hand on Catholic doctrine. The memorial highlights the union of learning, prayer, and holiness.

name: Saint John of Kanty, Priest
briefBio: Saint John of Kanty, Priest is commemorated in the Church calendar as optional memorial. The profile is available offline so the celebration can be opened directly from the Saint of the Day UI.

name: Saint Stephen, the First Martyr
briefBio: Saint Stephen, the First Martyr is remembered as a witness to Christ unto death. The memorial keeps before the Church the courage of fidelity under persecution.

name: Saint John, Apostle and Evangelist
briefBio: Saint John, Apostle and Evangelist is honored as an apostolic witness to Christ and the early mission of the Church. The celebration remembers the preaching, testimony, and faith handed on from the first generation of believers.

name: The Holy Innocents, Martyrs
briefBio: The Holy Innocents, Martyrs is remembered as a witness to Christ unto death. The memorial keeps before the Church the courage of fidelity under persecution.

name: Saint Thomas Becket
briefBio: Thomas Becket was Archbishop of Canterbury and a martyr for the freedom of the Church. His conflict with King Henry II ended with his murder in Canterbury Cathedral.

name: Saint Sylvester I, Pope
briefBio: Saint Sylvester I, Pope is honored for pastoral service to the Church as Bishop of Rome. The celebration recalls a life spent guarding faith, worship, and communion.

name: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary, and Joseph
briefBio: This feast honors Jesus, Mary, and Joseph as the Holy Family of Nazareth. It invites Christian families to contemplate hidden fidelity, work, prayer, and mutual love in ordinary domestic life.
feastDates: Sunday within the Octave of Christmas, or December 30 if no Sunday occurs

name: The Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary
briefBio: The Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary honors Mary under this feast, title, or mystery in the Church calendar. It invites devotion to her place in the life of Christ and her maternal care for the Church.
feastDates: Saturday after the Solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus

name: Mary, Mother of the Church
briefBio: This memorial honors Mary as Mother of the Church, a title rooted in her motherhood of Christ and her presence with the disciples at the birth of the Church. In Nigeria the readings are observed on the Monday after Pentecost.
